findings.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6 — Template now iterates `{{#each m in members}}` against the group-members route's controller, but no explicit GroupMembersController defining a `members` property exists in the repo (or was not included/verifiable); this only works if Ember's default generated controller for a non-array model is an ObjectController with implicit content-proxying to model.members (set async by findMembers) — could not verify this holds for this Discourse/Ember version's route setup, so there is a risk of `members` always resolving undefined

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:29 — GroupUserSerializer is referenced but not present in the reviewed file set, so it could not be confirmed the serializer output is unaffected by the new `members`/`meta` envelope (e.g. no accidental double-nesting or dropped fields)

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:24 — limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are used unvalidated in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`, so any caller (non-admin, only needs `guardian.ensure_can_see!` to pass) can request an arbitrarily large `limit` to dump an entire group's membership in one request (defeating the new default page size of 50) or pass a negative value that Postgres will reject with an unhandled `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` (minor DoS/error-based behavior)

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:120 — add_members` has no test for a non-existent username (old suite explicitly covered "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"); new spec only covers automatic-group rejection and the happy path with two real users

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:29 — GroupUserSerializer is referenced but not present in the reviewed file set, so it could not be confirmed the serializer output is unaffected by the new `members`/`meta` envelope (e.g. no accidental double-nesting or dropped fields)

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members, GroupUserSerializer)` (bare array response) to an explicit JSON envelope `{ members: serialize_data(...), meta: ... }`, and the client templates/routes are updated accordingly (e.g., `{{#each m in members}}` and `model.findMembers()` now sets `members` on the group model). The proposed finding is essentially “can’t confirm because serializer isn’t in this diff,” which is not a verifiable defect introduced by the change; there’s no evidence in the diff of double-nesting or dropped fields.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:24 — limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are used unvalidated in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`, so any caller (non-admin, only needs `guardian.ensure_can_see!` to pass) can request an arbitrarily large `limit` to dump an entire group's membership in one request (defeating the new default page size of 50) or pass a negative value that Postgres will reject with an unhandled `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` (minor DoS/error-based behavior)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and passes them directly into `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no bounds checking. This is verifiable in the diff. Negative values (e.g. offset = -1 or limit = -5) will be sent through to SQL (`OFFSET -1` / `LIMIT -5`), which PostgreSQL rejects, likely resulting in an uncaught `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` and a 500 response. The "arbitrarily large limit" concern is also true (no max), though the claim that it newly enables dumping the whole membership is weaker because the old code already returned all members for non-automatic groups (no limit at all).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:120 — add_members` has no test for a non-existent username (old suite explicitly covered "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"); new spec only covers automatic-group rejection and the happy path with two real users

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the prior incremental-update specs that explicitly asserted “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users,” and the new `.add_members` specs only cover automatic-group rejection and the happy path with real users. However, this is a test coverage regression rather than a verifiable bug/correctness defect introduced by the code: `add_members` still silently ignores unknown usernames via `if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`. The finding identifies missing test coverage, not a concrete defect in the implementation.
